title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): Building AI Tool Servers
objectives: Understand what MCP is and why it matters for enterprise AI
Build a basic MCP server that exposes tools to AI agents
Connect an MCP server to GitHub Copilot
Design tools that follow MCP best practices

sections.title: 🔍 What is MCP?
sections.content:
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard created by Anthropic that allows AI models to connect to external tools and data sources. Think of MCP as a "USB port for AI" — it provides a standardized way for any AI agent to use any tool, regardless of the vendor.

Without MCP, every AI tool integration is custom-built. With MCP, you build a tool server once and any MCP-compatible AI (Copilot, Claude, etc.) can use it.

💡 MCP Architecture

MCP Host: The AI application (e.g., VS Code with Copilot)
MCP Client: Protocol handler inside the host
MCP Server: Your custom tool server that exposes capabilities
Transport: Communication layer (stdio or HTTP/SSE)

questions.text: What is the best analogy for MCP?
options: A USB port for AI — standardized interface for connecting tools
questions.explanation: MCP is like a USB port — it provides a standardized interface so any AI model can connect to any tool, without custom integrations.

questions.text: Why does the MCP server example only allow SELECT queries?
options: Because MCP doesn't support other query types
To prevent the AI from accidentally modifying or deleting data
questions.explanation: Restricting to SELECT is a security best practice. AI agents should have read-only access to databases to prevent accidental data modification or deletion.

questions.text: What transport methods does MCP support?
questions.explanation: MCP supports stdio (standard input/output, good for local servers) and HTTP with Server-Sent Events (good for remote servers).

questions.text: What is the difference between an MCP Tool and an MCP Resource?
options: Tools perform actions with side effects; Resources provide read-only access to data
Resources can call APIs; Tools cannot
They are identical concepts with different names
questions.explanation: MCP Tools are executable functions that can have side effects (write to DB, send message, run command). MCP Resources are read-only data sources (file contents, DB records) — they expose data without triggering actions.

questions.text: Your mcp.json includes `requireApproval: ['run_terminal']`. An agent tries to run `rm -rf /tmp/build`. What happens?
options: Execution pauses and the user is prompted to approve or deny the terminal command
The agent silently skips the step
questions.explanation: requireApproval creates a human-in-the-loop checkpoint. Before executing any tool in the requireApproval list, the agent pauses and waits for explicit human confirmation — preventing accidental destructive operations.
